speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; to begin my assessment, have you noticed if these symptoms worsen when you move your head?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) - likely triggered by recent illness/motion, though the "constant" nature described is atypical and warrants exclusion of central causes or vestibular neuritis; however, given the age, lack of focal neuro deficits, and response to antihistamines, BPPV remains the most probable diagnosis pending exam confirmation.

REQUEST TEST: Dix-Hallpike maneuver
REQUEST IMAGES: None at this time.
